title: Quick Revision — Physical Quantities & Dimensions
notes: - **Physical quantity** = magnitude × unit; measurable property of matter/energy.
- **Seven SI base units:** m (length), kg (mass), s (time), K (temperature), A (current), mol (amount), cd (luminous intensity).
- **Derived quantities** are formed from base quantities (area, velocity, force, pressure, power).
- **Dimension symbols:** length [L], mass [M], time [T], temperature [K], current [A].
- **Dimensional formulas:** velocity [L T⁻¹], force [M L T⁻²], work [M L² T⁻²], pressure [M L⁻¹ T⁻²], power [M L² T⁻³], G [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²].
- **Uses of dimensional analysis:** check correctness of equations, derive relations (up to a constant), convert units n₁u₁ = n₂u₂.
- **Homogeneity rule:** only quantities of same dimensions may be added/equated.
- **Limitations:** cannot determine dimensionless constants, functions (trig/log/exp), or distinguish same-dimension quantities (work vs torque).
- **Significant figures:** non-zero digits + zeros between them are significant; leading zeros are not.
- **Errors:** absolute error = |value − mean|; relative = Δa/a; percentage = Δa/a × 100%.
- **Scientific notation** a × 10ⁿ (1 ≤ a < 10); **order of magnitude** is the nearest power of ten.
